data.name: Vedanarayan
data.gender_notes: Vedanarayan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Veda (Knowledge) and Narayan (The Ultimate Reality). The name Vedanarayan carries the meaning “God of Knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vedanarayan usually hope their child will grow to embody god of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the pursuit of spiritual wisdom and truth.
data.etymology: Vedanarayan belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vedanarayan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.spiritual_significance: Vedanarayan is a name that holds profound spiritual significance in Hinduism. Narayan is a common name for Vishnu, the preserver deity in Hinduism, who is believed to be the ultimate reality and supreme god. Vedanarayan, therefore, represents the embodiment of both knowledge (Veda) and the ultimate reality (Narayan). This name signifies a deep connection to the divine, a seeker of knowledge and spiritual truth, and a lifelong pursuit of enlightenment and happiness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vedanarayan translates to 'God of Blissful Wisdom'. It symbolizes the pursuit of knowledge and spiritual enlightenment, while being guided by the divine and experiencing ultimate joy and happiness.

vedic_reference.note: Narayana is a name for Lord Vishnu. Veda refers to knowledge.

historical_references.reference: According to the Puranas, Vedanarayan is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu and is often depicted as the presiding deity of the sacred Triveni Sangam, the confluence of three holy rivers - the Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati. This is a popular belief in Hinduism and is widely celebrated in various parts of India.

Vedanarayan was also the name of a renowned philosopher and scholar in medieval India, who lived in the 14th century CE. He was a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement and is believed to have written several works on Hinduism, including commentaries on the Vedas and the Bhagavad Gita.
